title: Design a 1B-Event Real-Time Unique User & Ad-Attribution Analytics Pipeline
prompt: Design a real-time analytics and ad-attribution pipeline that computes COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) across 1,000,000,000+ daily events and 100+ segmented metrics with sub-second dashboard queries, multi-day rollups, and bounded cluster memory.

spark.summary: Replace 64 GB/metric exact HashSets with partitioned Flink/Kafka HyperLogLog sketches (1.5–12 KB each) merged via O(m) element-wise MAX into ClickHouse/Redis rollups.
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, 100 concurrent billion-scale metrics shrink from 6.4 TB of RAM to 150 KB–1.2 MB while supporting instant hourly-to-monthly rollups.
spark.byteSummary:
Scale Bottleneck: Exact distinct counting over 1B daily UUIDs consumes ~64 GB RAM per metric (6.4 TB for 100 metrics) and forces O(N) network shuffles during cross-shard unions.

Core Architecture: Edge/Flink workers maintain per-window HyperLogLog sketches (p=11 for 1.5 KB or p=14 for 12 KB) in local state, flushing compact register arrays to ClickHouse (`uniqCombined` / `AggregateFunction(uniqHLL12)`) or Redis (`PFADD`/`PFMERGE`) every 10–60 seconds.

Rollup & Accuracy Strategy: Hourly sketches merge in O(m) time via element-wise MAX to answer arbitrary multi-day queries in sub-10ms with <1–2.3% standard error, while sparse encoding prevents memory bloat on long-tail campaigns.

learningJourney.title: Capacity Sizing: 6.4 TB Exact Sets vs 150 KB HLL Sketches
learningJourney.purpose: Compare memory and network shuffle costs across 100 metrics at 1B+ events/day.

explanation.foundation: At 1B unique users/day (~11,500 new uniques/sec, 50k+ total events/sec), retaining raw 64-byte UUID entries costs 64 GB per metric. With HyperLogLog at `p = 11` (1.5 KB) or `p = 14` (12 KB), 100 metrics occupy only 150 KB to 1.2 MB total—fitting entirely inside L3 CPU cache.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Design a 1B-Event Real-Time Unique User & Ad-Attribution Analytics Pipeline, watch how capacity sizing: 6.4 tb exact sets vs 150 kb hll sketches interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Production billion-event pipelines combine sparse-to-dense HLL promotion, 64-bit hash-seed versioning, and nightly 1% exact audits with 3-sigma alerting.

learningJourney.title: Stream Ingestion & Partition-Local Pre-Aggregation
learningJourney.purpose: Avoid expensive key-by-user_id shuffles by aggregating HLL sketches locally on every Kafka/Flink partition.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Stream Ingestion & Partition-Local Pre-Aggregation** as the intuition layer for Design a 1B-Event Real-Time Unique User & Ad-Attribution Analytics Pipeline: Avoid expensive key-by-user_id shuffles by aggregating HLL sketches locally on every Kafka/Flink partition.
explanation.core: An exact `COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)` in Spark/Flink usually forces a global `GROUP BY metric_id, user_id` shuffle across the cluster. Because HyperLogLog is mergeable, each Flink worker updates a **partition-local** HLL sketch for `(metric_id, 1-minute_bucket)` with zero network shuffle per event, emitting only the 1.5 KB sketch at window close!
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, stream ingestion & partition-local pre-aggregation becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production billion-event pipelines combine sparse-to-dense HLL promotion, 64-bit hash-seed versioning, and nightly 1% exact audits with 3-sigma alerting.

decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.

learningJourney.title: Hierarchical Time-Bucket Rollups (Minute -> Hour -> Day)
learningJourney.purpose: Enable sub-10ms arbitrary date-range unique counts (e.g., 7-day or 30-day uniques) via pre-merged HLL rollups.

explanation.foundation: You cannot sum daily unique counts to get weekly uniques (users repeat across days).
explanation.core: Instead, store 1-minute HLL sketches in ClickHouse (`AggregateFunction(uniqHLL12)`) or Redis, and run background `PFMERGE` rollups into hourly and daily HLL rows.
explanation.deepDive: A 30-day dashboard query simply merges 30 daily 1.5 KB sketches in < 1 ms!

learningJourney.title: Precision Tuning: 1.5 KB (2.3% err) vs 12 KB (0.81% err)
learningJourney.purpose: Choose register precision p based on billing-grade vs operational-dashboard accuracy requirements.

explanation.core: For real-time anomaly dashboards, `p = 11` (2,048 registers, 1.5 KB, 2.3% error) is ideal.
explanation.deepDive: For ad-tech billing or SLA reporting, `p = 14` (16,384 registers, 12 KB, 0.81% error) or `p = 16` (65,536 registers, 48 KB, 0.40% error) trades a few extra kilobytes for sub-1% precision.

cards.label: 3-Sigma Bound
cards.detail: At p=14 (0.81% sigma), 99.7% of estimates fall within +/- 2.43% of exact truth.

sectionDiagram.summary: Caption: Increasing precision p by 2 bits quadruples register memory while halving standard error.
sectionDiagram.caption: Caption: Increasing precision p by 2 bits quadruples register memory while halving standard error.

learningJourney.title: Handling Long-Tail Segmented Metrics with Sparse Encoding
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent OOM when users slice dashboards by high-cardinality dimensions (e.g., 5M distinct URLs or ads).

explanation.foundation: If analysts group by `ad_id` (5 million ads), 90% of ads receive fewer than 50 clicks/day.
explanation.core: Allocating 12 KB dense HLLs for 5M keys would take 60 GB!
explanation.deepDive: Use **sparse HLL encoding** (storing a sorted list of `(bucket, rho)` 32-bit integers) until sparse size reaches 50% of dense size, cutting total memory by > 85%.

learningJourney.title: Idempotent Checkpointing & Exact-Once Sketch Durability
learningJourney.purpose: Ensure worker restarts or Kafka replays do not corrupt sketches or lose window state.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Idempotent Checkpointing & Exact-Once Sketch Durability** as the intuition layer for Design a 1B-Event Real-Time Unique User & Ad-Attribution Analytics Pipeline: Ensure worker restarts or Kafka replays do not corrupt sketches or lose window state.
explanation.core: Because `PFADD` / `max(regs[idx], rho)` is **idempotent**, replaying a duplicate Kafka message for the same `user_id` leaves the HLL sketch completely unchanged! Pairing Flink incremental RocksDB checkpoints with idempotent `MERGE` upserts into ClickHouse/Redis guarantees at-least-once replays produce exact HLL convergence.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, idempotent checkpointing & exact-once sketch durability becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production billion-event pipelines combine sparse-to-dense HLL promotion, 64-bit hash-seed versioning, and nightly 1% exact audits with 3-sigma alerting.

learningJourney.title: Observability, Hash-Drift Guards & Billing Reconciliation
learningJourney.purpose: Detect silent hash-seed mismatches and reconcile probabilistic estimates against nightly exact batch audits.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Observability, Hash-Drift Guards & Billing Reconciliation** as the intuition layer for Design a 1B-Event Real-Time Unique User & Ad-Attribution Analytics Pipeline: Detect silent hash-seed mismatches and reconcile probabilistic estimates against nightly exact batch audits.
explanation.core: Because HLL errors are bounded and predictable (`~1.04 / sqrt(m)`), run a nightly Spark/SQL exact `COUNT(DISTINCT)` audit on a 1% sampled metric set. Alert if observed drift exceeds `3 * sigma` (which immediately catches hash-seed mismatches, truncated 32-bit hashes, or corrupted sparse-to-dense merges).
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, observability, hash-drift guards & billing reconciliation becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. knowledgeChecks.question: In a Flink + Kafka pipeline computing COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) for 100 campaign metrics, why does HyperLogLog eliminate the need to shuffle raw events by user_id?

options.text: Kafka automatically deduplicates user_id across all partitions.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Kafka partitions do not globally deduplicate distinct keys across topics.

options.text: Each partition updates a tiny local HLL sketch and emits only the 1.5–12 KB sketch at window close for O(m) PFMERGE.
options.feedback: Correct: Local HLL accumulation plus O(m) element-wise MAX merging removes the global user_id shuffle.

options.text: Flink stores all 1B user IDs in Redis instead.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Storing 1B raw IDs in Redis would still consume 64 GB per metric.

options.text: HyperLogLog only counts total events, not unique users.
options.feedback: Incorrect: HyperLogLog specifically estimates unique cardinality.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Partition-local HLL sketches can be merged via O(m) element-wise MAX without ever shuffling raw user_id records.

knowledgeChecks.question: Your ad-tech platform tracks 5,000,000 ad_id segments, 90% of which see fewer than 30 clicks/day. How do you avoid spending 60 GB of RAM on 12 KB dense HLL arrays?

options.text: Drop all ads with fewer than 30 clicks.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Dropping long-tail ads loses attribution data.
Incorrect: A 4-bit hash cannot distinguish more than 16 buckets.

options.text: Start each key in a sparse HLL representation (~100 bytes) and promote to dense 12 KB only when sparse entries exceed the threshold.
options.feedback: Correct: Sparse-to-dense promotion cuts long-tail RAM by ~85–90% while preserving exact HLL accuracy.

options.text: Store raw UUIDs in a SQL table in RAM.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Raw UUIDs still scale linearly with N.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Sparse HLL encoding stores only non-zero (bucket, rho) pairs for low-cardinality keys before promoting to dense arrays.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is HyperLogLog naturally resilient to at-least-once Kafka message replays after a worker crash?

options.text: Because updating regs[idx] = max(regs[idx], rho) is idempotent—replaying the same user_id produces the identical hash and leaves registers unchanged.
options.feedback: Correct: Duplicate deliveries of the same user_id yield the same (idx, rho) and never inflate the sketch.

options.text: Because HLL resets all registers to zero on every restart.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Resetting registers would lose all historical counts.

options.text: Because HLL increments a counter by +1 on every event.
options.feedback: Incorrect: HLL takes the max leading-zero run, not a sum.

options.text: Because Kafka deletes duplicates before consumers read.
options.feedback: Incorrect: At-least-once consumers can still receive duplicate deliveries on restart.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Since HLL updates registers via max(regs[idx], rho) on deterministic hashes, duplicate event replays are idempotent.

prerequisites.title: HyperLogLog & Probabilistic Cardinality Estimation
prerequisites.summary: HyperLogLog hashes each element into 64 bits, routes it to one of m = 2^p registers, tracks the maximum leading-zero run rho(w), and averages registers via a bias-corrected harmonic mean in O(1) space.
